patch.value: A wrong-typed member in schema/statuses.json or schema/types.json (a numeric description, a numeric alias) throws in its normalizer and resets every setting to its default

Found 2026-11-27 while fixing pm-x9r2h3. loadRuntimeSchemaFromOptionalFiles now skips status and field entries that are not objects and type entries without a string name, but the status and type normalizers still call trim on members they assume are strings: a status with description 5, or a type with description 5 or aliases [5], throws inside the settings read, which then fails its merge (settings_read_merge_failed) and every setting falls back to its default. The field normalizer was hardened in pm-x9r2h3 (non-string description is ignored and reported); statuses and types need the same treatment, plus a validate report of what was ignored. Reproduced on the built CLI by calling normalizeRuntimeSchemaSettings with statuses [{ id: 'x', description: 5 }] and normalizeItemTypeDefinitions with [{ name: 'X', description: 5 }]. Duplicate check: searched statuses types normalizer description crash settings_read_merge_failed; no open item covers it.

A status or type schema file entry with any wrong-typed member no longer fails the settings read; the member is ignored and the rest of the entry and of the settings load; pm validate or pm health names each ignored member with its file and position; A spec seeds wrong-typed members for every string and list member of a status and a type definition, with a negative control on the current release
One malformed member in a schema file cannot reset every setting
settings_read_merge_failed and defaults for the whole tracker
